title: Anterior placenta percreta (prior cesareans): greatest risk of invasion into the bladder
vignette: A 38-year-old woman, gravida 4 para 3, at 18 weeks gestation comes to the office for a routine anatomy ultrasound. The patient has had no vaginal bleeding, leakage of fluid, or contractions. She has no chronic medical conditions and her 3 prior pregnancies resulted in uncomplicated cesarean deliveries. Blood pressure is 118/66 mm Hg and pulse is 94/min. Fundal height is appropriate for gestational age. Transabdominal ultrasound reveals a fetus measuring 18 weeks gestation, an amniotic fluid index of 8 cm (normal: >5 cm), and an anterior placenta that covers the internal cervical os and penetrates the uterine myometrium. This patient is at greatest risk of placental invasion into which of the following structures?

clues.text: 3 prior pregnancies resulted in uncomplicated cesarean deliveries
clues.note: Prior cesarean scars create thin myometrium lacking decidua basalis - the setting for abnormal placental implantation (placenta accreta spectrum) and placenta previa.

clues.text: anterior placenta that covers the internal cervical os and penetrates the uterine myometrium
clues.note: An ANTERIOR placenta covering the os that penetrates the myometrium is placenta percreta (invasion through the myometrium/serosa); anterior location puts the adjacent BLADDER at risk.

whatMatters: An ANTERIOR PLACENTA PERCRETA (invasion through the myometrium) over prior cesarean scars is positioned just behind the BLADDER (the structure immediately anterior to the uterus), so it is at greatest risk of invading the BLADDER. Answer A.
strategy: Localize by placental position: an ANTERIOR percreta invades the structure ANTERIOR to the uterus = the bladder (risk of hematuria/hemorrhage). Reject lateral/posterior/adnexal structures that an anterior placenta wouldn't reach: broad ligament, infundibulopelvic and uterosacral ligaments (lateral/posterior), the cervix (dense fibrous tissue, resistant to invasion), and the ureter (lateral/posterior course).

eliminations.label: Broad ligament - lateral, lower risk
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a lateral peritoneal fold containing the round/uteroovarian ligaments and tube. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it extends LATERALLY from the uterus, so an anterior placenta is unlikely to invade it. ✅ Correct if: lateral uterine invasion.

eliminations.label: Cervix - dense, resistant tissue
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the fibromuscular lower uterine outlet. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: although the placenta covers the os, the cervix is dense, firm connective tissue that resists penetration compared with the myometrium. ✅ Correct if: placenta previa with cervical implantation (rare invasion).

eliminations.label: Infundibulopelvic ligament - lateral (ovarian vessels)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the suspensory ligament of the ovary carrying the ovarian vessels to the pelvic sidewall. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is lateral to the uterus, away from an anterior placenta. ✅ Correct if: lateral pelvic/ovarian vessel involvement.

eliminations.label: Uterosacral ligament - posterior anchor
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a ligament anchoring the posterior uterus to the sacrum. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is posterior, whereas the placenta here is anterior. ✅ Correct if: posterior uterine invasion.

eliminations.label: Ureter - lateral/posterior course
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the tube conveying urine along the lateral pelvic sidewall to the bladder. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: its course is posterolateral to the uterus, making invasion by an anterior placenta unlikely. ✅ Correct if: lateral pelvic invasion near the ureter.

reasoning: Prior cesarean scars predispose to abnormal placental implantation over thin, decidua-poor myometrium
An anterior placenta covering the os that penetrates the myometrium = placenta percreta
The bladder lies immediately anterior to the uterus
-> an anterior percreta is at greatest risk of invading the bladder; answer A
mechanism: The PLACENTA ACCRETA SPECTRUM is defined by the DEPTH of abnormal placental invasion: placenta ACCRETA (attaches to the myometrium), INCRETA (invades INTO the myometrium), and PERCRETA (penetrates THROUGH the myometrium and serosa into adjacent structures). The most common site is over a PRIOR UTERINE (cesarean) SCAR, where thin myometrium lacks the DECIDUA BASALIS needed to form a normal cleavage plane. Repeat cesareans produce an anterior, low transverse scar, so future placentas tend to implant ANTERIORLY and LOW, often covering the internal cervical os (placenta previa). An invasive ANTERIOR placenta can breach the uterine wall and grow into the structure immediately ANTERIOR to the uterus - the URINARY BLADDER - risking hematuria and catastrophic hemorrhage at delivery. The other listed structures are lateral (broad ligament, infundibulopelvic ligament, ureter) or posterior (uterosacral ligament), and the cervix is dense fibrous tissue resistant to invasion. Therefore the bladder is at greatest risk.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid OB/Anatomy > placenta accreta spectrum: accreta (attach), increta (into myometrium), percreta (through serosa into adjacent organs); risk = prior cesarean/uterine scar (decidua-poor); anterior percreta -> bladder invasion; risk of hemorrhage.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Anterior placenta percreta over cesarean scars -> invades the bladder (immediately anterior structure).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on placenta accreta/increta/percreta, decidua basalis, placenta previa, or myometrium? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Broad/infundibulopelvic/uterosacral ligaments and ureter are lateral/posterior; cervix is dense/resistant.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: anterior placenta percreta invades the bladder; posterior/lateral structures are lower risk.

keywords.front: Major risk factor for accreta spectrum

keywords.back: Placenta covering the internal cervical os

firstAid.detail: OB: anterior invasion -> bladder; prior cesareans.
OB > depth of invasion; decidua basalis defect.

memoryHook: An anterior placenta that eats through the uterus (percreta) runs straight into what's in front - the bladder.
